outcome.technical: REPRODUCED: a scratch driver ran cl5's body (_signal_mid_run with SIGTERM) in a loop against one fixture repo. Before the fix: 2/200 idle; 7/200, 13/200 and 7/150 under 12 CPU burners on a 10-cpu darwin host. Every survivor was the TASK leg's process (its TMPDIR named task-tmp-), never the baseline's; helper exit 0.04-0.12 s after the signal. A scratch copy of the plugin, instrumented to dump the KeyboardInterrupt traceback, placed every hit inside the main thread's subprocess.Popen in _run_in: at _fork_exec's return, in the os.read of the exec pipe, in _close_pipe_fds, or on Popen's return before `proc` was bound. CAUSE: the task leg runs on the main thread; Python raises the signal's exception there between any two bytecodes, so one landing after the fork but before _run_in held the process skipped _run_in's teardown (Popen sat outside the try), and the main thread's own run is in no `live` list in _concurrent_legs. The process, in its own session (setsid), outlived the helper. The fault was in the product, not the case: cl5 stays the same hard assertion. FIX (stamp-verification.py): new _spawn_held starts the run from a thread of its own (no signal exception is raised there), into a holder dict, under a lock; _run_in now keeps the spawn, started(proc) and communicate in one try, and its BaseException arm takes the lock, sets cancelled and tears down whatever process the holder has, so the stop either cancels the start or waits for it and tears the run down. This covers every _run_in call (baseline, task, task-held, task-support, second, fix), not only the concurrent pair. The join poll became the constant JOIN_SLICE, shared with _concurrent_legs. TEST: il5 in _interrupted_leg_cases (stage sr-interrupted-legs) swaps subprocess.Popen for one that, once the real process exists, sends SIGTERM to the thread that spawned it (signal.pthread_kill), with the interrupt handlers armed, then calls M._run_in. Before the fix: FAIL il5 ... interrupt raised 'SIGTERM', returned None, processes made [37077], alive after `_run_in` raised [37077] (4/5). After the fix: PASS, alive [] (5/5). It adds no literal clock figure, so sk1 needs no row (passed in the gate). Skipped on Windows (no pthread_kill). RE-MEASURED with the same loop and a stricter second read 0.5 s after the helper exits: 0/200 idle; 0/200 loaded; 0/200 loaded again after a ~6-minute gap. GATE: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py exit 0, 1/1 files ok, 410 cases. Also run: tests/test__proc_group.py sweep exit 0 (39 cases; its pin on the names _run_in calls still holds); ruff, vermin -t=3.8-, release.py changelog-check, and the --register-citations pre-gate, all exit 0. DOCS: PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's stamp-verification section gains the spawn-window paragraph; changelog.d/P174.5-njh.fixed.md added. DEPENDANTS: tests/test_stamp_verification.py: sweep-costs.json, test__affected_tests.py, test__filed_returns.py, tools/affected.py, tools/sweep-selftests.py, tools/verify.sh and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md are still correct, because no name they use changed (_cli, _crlf_cases, _git and _scan are untouched) and the new case sits in an existing stage. stamp-verification.py: _run_in's signature and return contract are unchanged and _concurrent_legs is untouched apart from JOIN_SLICE, so test__claude_home, test__filed_returns, test__proc_group (passes), test_audit_lookup, test_audit_task, test_drive_phase, tools/affected.py and _filed_returns.py's prose mention are still correct. LEFT, class outside this task's files: run-test-gate.py (_shell) and run-agent-session.py also arm the same interrupt and start process groups with Popen on the main thread, so the same spawn window is open there (inferred from the code; not reproduced). Lifting _spawn_held into _proc_group.py would close it for every reader, and that file is not in this task. Also noted: three held-command processes from earlier cl5 runs were already on this machine before my loops started (etime 43 min to 9 h), consistent with this survivor. I left them running because they are not mine.
outcome.descriptive: A SIGTERM that lands while a red-first leg is starting its process no longer leaves that process alive after the helper exits. The cl5 hit rate went from 1-9% to 0 in 600 runs.
